Q: no math module python A:

As an alternative, here's how you would install xlwt with Python 2.4 locally:

python setup.py build
python setup.py install --prefix=${HOME}/.local

Note that the .local directory is the default one used by the --user option in Python 2.6/7.

This install xlwt, but doesn't let you run it. Now, you'll need to set your PYTHONPATH correctly:

export PYTHONPATH=${HOME}/.local/lib/python2.4/site-packages

This assumes a (ba)sh type shell.

Since you would need to do this everytime you run python in a new shell, you're better off setting your PYTHONPATH in a shell source file.

And, of course, if there is already a PYTHONPATH set ($ echo $PYTHONPATH will show you), it would be

export PYTHONPATH=${PYTHONPATH}:${HOME}/.local/lib/python2.4/site-packages

Q: Enforcing a 2 second delay on Web API call? A:

Basic OS timers aren't that accurate. If you aren't displaying video frames, you don't need that level of accuracy.

Q: Can't get the new `relevantDates` object to work with apple wallet pass on iOS 18.6.x A:

For what I was able to see while developing passkit-generator, it seems that each relevantDates record can be of a time span up to 24h, from 00:00:00 to 23:59:59. Which means that startDate and endDate must have the same day.

I know I'm a bit late, but I feel like this might be the reason.

Q: Use @Pattern to validate UUID or UUID.toString() A:

UUID != String

You must understand that a UUID is not text. A java.util.UUID object is not a String object. A UUID is a 128-bit value where some of the bits have special meaning per the standard spec.

Humans do not do well with reading/writing 128 bits, such as one hundred and twenty eight 0 & 1 digits.

1010 1111 0111 0000 0000 0101 1001 1100

1111 0110 0000 0100 0100 1100 1011 1101

1001 1101 0010 0111 0010 1100 1111 1111

0111 1110 0010 1000 0000 1011 0001 0011

So when presenting a UUID for human consumption we translate the 128-bit value to a hexadecimal string of 32 characters. Canonically those hex characters are grouped with four hyphens, for a total of 36 characters.

Example per UuidGenerator.net:

af70059c-f604-4cbd-9d27-2cff7e280b13

Such a hex string is not a UUID, it represents a UUID value, a handy way to read or write 128 bits.

If you have a UUID object at hand in Java, you need not do any validation. Indeed, you have no string against which to do any validation. So regex is irrelevant. You have only 128-bits, stored internally as a pair of 64-bit integer numbers in most implementations.

To validate an incoming string in canonical format, there is no need for your pattern to validate, just parse using the java.util.UUID class and trap for exception.

If you do suspect invalid UUID input, you will need to look outside the classes bundled with Java. The java.util.UUID.fromString method does only basic validation. The implementation in OpenJDK checks for the expected four HYPHEN-MINUS characters, and checks for more than the expected 36 characters, but nothing more. There are at least two Java libraries for managing UUIDs. Perhaps one of those may do more thorough validation.

Case

By the way, the former UUID standard spec (RFC 4122) requires any hex representation to be generated in all lowercase, while tolerating uppercase/mixedcase when parsing. This rule is violated by many implementations including those by Apple and by Microsoft. The current spec, RFC 9562, gave up on the issue, allowing for lowercase, uppercase, or mixedcase.

Q: Can't use echo on data created by CodeIgniter's result() method A:

Are you sure you are returning something from your model's total_count function ... as per your listing there is no return statement which means null will be echoed resulting in blank.

Just selecting will not make the model returns the query result, you need to return explicitly

Please try to var_dump($totalcount) to see what is in your result set as this is a result set not a value according to your query.

Q: How To Copy Formulas Only In Google Sheets (without values or formatting) in few steps? A:

Surprisingly easy solution (but shameful that it is necessary) and works for copies across many columns or rows.

Ctrl + ~ to expose the formulas

Ctrl+H and select 'Also search within formulas'

Replace the '=' with another character not used in your formula (like '#')

Copy the the cells containing formulas you want

Then Ctrl+H select search 'Also search within formulas' and replace that swapped character with the equal sign.
